summary: A modular monolith on Google Cloud Run using NestJS with Supabase Postgres and a React Native (Expo) client. Chosen for an intermediate team of 3 with a $150/month budget and 30,000 users in 12 months.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) targets android, ios, web, covering project.platforms=[web, android]. It reuses the team's skills (team.languages=[javascript, python, typescript]). requirements.seo_critical=true: client-side rendering is weak for SEO, so add pre-rendering for public pages.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 1.1 points lower: weaker on cost efficiency (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 4/5).
Ranked 1.2 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 4 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 5/5).

tradeoffs: Native modules can force ejecting from the managed workflow
what_would_change: If the target platforms change (today [web, android]), re-check coverage: Next.js is the next option.
If SEO stopped being critical and the app became highly interactive, a SPA framework would become competitive.

backend.justification: The team already knows javascript, typescript (team.languages=[javascript, python, typescript]), which NestJS uses. A team.experience=intermediate team of team.size=3 gets NestJS's typed, structured API model (operations burden 2 vs capacity 2). NestJS handles websocket connections for requirements.realtime=true. It can meet the requirements.p95_latency_ms=500 ms p95 target on Google Cloud Run. It supports an MVP within timeline.mvp_weeks=8 weeks given its rating of 4/5 for time to market.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.3 points lower: weaker on maintainability (rated 3 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5).
Ranked 0.4 points lower: weaker on performance (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 3/5).

tradeoffs: Opinionated and verbose for tiny services
Node single-thread limits for CPU-bound work
what_would_change: If the team changed languages (today [javascript, python, typescript]), re-rank: Express is the next best fit.
If scale.users_12_months passed 3,000,000, NestJS would need horizontal scaling and caching (cap = its comfortable range).

database.justification: Supabase Postgres suits scale.workload=balanced traffic with scale.data_volume_gb_12_months=50 GB after 12 months. requirements.full_text_search=true: it has built-in full-text search, so no separate search engine is added at this scale. For infrastructure.data_residency=india: it can run in Supabase South Asia (Mumbai, ap-south-1) to satisfy data_residency=india. It is acceptable under compliance=[dpdp] as a managed service whose vendor reports you should review. Its comfortable range (1,000,000 users) covers scale.users_12_months=30000. requirements.payments=true: transactional integrity favours a relational engine.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.6 points lower: weaker on cost efficiency (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 4/5); costs more (about $22-160/mo vs $9-100).
Ranked 2.0 points lower: weaker on maintainability (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 3/5).

tradeoffs: Smaller operator than hyperscalers; plan limits apply

what_would_change: If users exceeded 1,000,000, add read replicas or caching, or shard.
If requirements.offline_support became true, a store with device sync (Firestore or CouchDB) would gain priority.

hosting.justification: Google Cloud Run fits the monthly budget (budget.monthly_infra_usd=150 USD): estimated $6-90/month at scale.users_12_months=30000. For infrastructure.data_residency=india: it can run in Google Cloud Mumbai (asia-south1) or Delhi (asia-south2) to satisfy data_residency=india. It is compatible with compliance=[dpdp]; the legal obligations remain with you. A p95 target of requirements.p95_latency_ms=500 ms is realistic here. It supports persistent websocket connections (requirements.realtime=true). Operations burden 2 vs team capacity 2 (team.has_devops=false, team.experience=intermediate).

assumptions: Order-of-magnitude band built from each component's fixed + per-1k-user price estimate at scale.users_12_months=30,000; not a quote.
Traffic pattern steady adds no burst allowance.
The upper bound assumes components are not all at their high estimates at once (60% of the summed spread). Excludes taxes, engineers' time, payment-gateway transaction fees and SMS/OTP fees.

warnings.message: React Native (Expo) renders on the client, which is weak for SEO although requirements.seo_critical=true; pre-render or server-render the public pages (for example a separate marketing site).
The upper cost band ($194) exceeds the budget ($150); the lower band ($16) fits.
Google Cloud Memorystore (cache) was left out to respect budget.monthly_infra_usd=150; revisit it as traffic grows.

assumptions: Relaxed (budget): the optional cache component (Google Cloud Memorystore) was deferred to keep the estimate near the budget; add it when usage grows.
compliance_notes: DPDP Act (India): collect verifiable consent, honour access/erasure rights and notify breaches; the DPDP Act does not by itself require in-country storage, but the chosen India-capable regions keep options open.
Data residency india: primary data stores and hosting were limited to india-capable options (it can run in Google Cloud Mumbai (asia-south1) or Delhi (asia-south2) to satisfy data_residency=india).
